A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LiTEx study, taxonomy, e-SNLI data and core experiments. All pages, including appendices, support comparison; relocated and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original taxonomy annotations, inter-annotator agreement, classifier evaluations, explanation-generation comparisons and semantic-coverage results.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds human validation of 8,373 GPT-4o explanations, plus further classification and annotation error analyses.

M1.justification: The eight taxonomy categories, decision criteria, classification procedures and two-stage/end-to-end generation methods are retained. Changing Logical Structure Conflict to Logic Conflict is a terminology edit, not a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,002 e-SNLI items with 3,108 segmented explanations and 67 additional items for taxonomy agreement. The added validation examines outputs from the retained tasks; ANLI and LiveNLI remain proposed future extensions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the classification and generation experiments, including random/majority baselines, BERT/RoBERTa, prompted LLMs, and label-only/highlight-guided generation. LoRA fine-tuning and human-versus-model highlight comparisons already appear in v1.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 introduces a substantial new evaluation protocol: one trained annotator assesses 8,373 GPT-4o two-stage explanations using separate binary judgments of NLI-label consistency and taxonomy consistency. Existing splits, training configurations and automatic scoring procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds category-specific generation validation in Appendix G, three human annotation-disagreement cases in Appendix B, and a GPT-4o confusion matrix with two classification-error cases in Appendix C. These substantially expand diagnostics of category boundaries and generation failures beyond v1's aggregate validation and retained prompting analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed evaluations, confidence intervals or significance tests. The existing descriptive boxplots are retained; the new validation counts and percentages do not introduce uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: New human-validation results report 98.27% label consistency and 83.84% taxonomy consistency, with substantial category differences, including 57.25% for Coreference and 94.88% for Syntactic. V3 also adds classification-confusion results and generation-count averages. Main Tables 2, 4 and 5 and the detailed generation scores are unchanged; v1's separate per-category IAA summary table is removed.

T1.justification: Section 5's explicit binary wording for full coverage restates v1's requirement that every human reference point lie inside the model-output convex hull. The coverage definitions are otherwise unchanged, and neither version contains theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction explicitly restrict the taxonomy's scope to English explanations. The central claims about capturing within-label variation, taxonomy learnability and improved human alignment through taxonomy-guided generation remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 qualifies conciseness benefits as primarily two-stage-specific, relates coverage differences to output quantity, and explains highlight disagreement partly through annotation-task differences. Appendices B, C and G substantially expand category-boundary and failure explanations. Some new interpretations overreach: Appendix C calls Absence of Mention classification highly reliable although Figure 7 shows only 44 of 94 examples classified correctly.

D1.justification: V3 identifies Sentence-BERT as the embedding source and clarifies constraints in the existing highlight-agreement study. The repository footnote changes from a promised release to claimed public availability, although the conclusion retains future-release wording. Hardware, hyperparameters and substantive prompt instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Jayaweera and Dorr (2025), Chen et al.'s Threading the Needle (2025), and Sentence-BERT, and explicitly credits Jiang and de Marneffe (2022) as a foundation for the categorization. The broader positioning remains stable; publication and bibliographic updates to retained works are not new research coverage.

P1.justification: Targeted editing standardizes category terminology, updates author affiliations and revises several explanatory passages. Section 4.3 and Appendix G are added and Appendices B-C expanded, while the overall section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds the GPT-4o confusion matrix (Figure 7) and human-validation table (Table 17), removes v1's IAA summary Table 9, and relocates several appendix tables nearer their discussions. Existing main figures and tables retain essentially the same visual design.

improvement.justification: V3 adds direct human validation of explanation correctness and taxonomy adherence, addressing a gap in v1's automatic similarity/coverage evaluation, and provides useful failure analyses and qualifications. The gain is limited by auditing one GPT-4o configuration with one annotator and no human-rated baselines. New Appendix C also overstates classification reliability and misattributes the 0.492 macro-F1 setting relative to Table 12, tempering the overall improvement.
